text:
Delay of four hours. I got to the airport 2 hours early. Customary. The airport is 12 gates. Small, regional. There was a smoothie place next to mine. The smoothie was okay. I bought a quesadilla with it. The egg and sausage in it reminded of a lesser Duncan. The salsa with it was essentially a politely spicy ketchup.

The Asheville Regional Airport was redone completely in the 4.5 years since I'd been away. There used to be one restaurant that served burgers, and local beers on tap. Now there's a Jimmy John's, the smoothie place, a bar/grill, and a sundries place. There are mostly the hard plastic chairs typical of any airport, but there are now 8 large, cushioned chairs with high backs and individual charging stations, which look like little isolation stations, first class in the terminal, before you get on the plane, always full.

The internet connection is acceptable.

I nip between my seat in the terminal and the handicapped stall in the men's room next to me, where I take about 3 puffs on my flavorless vape once every 30 minutes. I will not cold turkey today. I will simply puff at this rate until I can finally pass out on the plane for 2 hours. I am resolved against drinking. I've read 100 pages of Fall of Hyperion. I cannot think of what to write.

I've had a week back in Asheville, NC. First time I've been back in 4.5 years, really the first opportunity I've had to return in all that time. I spent the time doing Nothing, about as much nothing as I possibly could. I've slept 12 hours on 4 of my 8 days out here. My bed was comfortable, the most comfortable sleeping arrangement I've had in years. It was situated in a condominium in the tallest structure in downtown Asheville, hotel vibes (it was in a hotel after all), had a full kitchen with a gas range, 2 tvs, proximity to a grocery co-op. I blew cash on food and massage primarily.

I'd an enormous rented pickup truck. I intended a 4-door sedan, something small and a little fast if possible, but by the time I arrived, they were out of those. They did have a massive GMC Sierra. So, driving for the first time in ~4 years, they gave me this behemoth to roam the mountains in the night, in light rain. I was pleased. A touch daunted, but pleased. Something to the image of it in my head.

New York is exhausting. It is an exhausting city, up all night, with no proper sense of relaxation. It pairs accurately with my job, which is up all hours of the night, with no proper sense of relaxation. I came here to sleep, and I accomplished that, though I still nurse my recent nicotine addiction. A proper bitch to quit, worse while working a job, all the worse a busy one. Frayed mind demands so much sleep.

Nicotine also provides me some illusion of satiety, which no other stimulant seems to. It actively quiets the mind. The frayed overtired sensation you get when quitting pairs with a resurgence of thoughts that veer racing. A funny way to inspire urgency, all the funnier when it sends me to the bathroom to suck on my joyless, flavorless gray Juul, a device I've deliberately chosen to combat the exciting, tasty fidget I'd previously discovered in the AirBar (a truly addictive, dangerous device which I'll look back fondly on for the rest of my life).

---------

Just had an hourlong conversation with the woman across from me. She's flying into Newark too, but has a long drive ahead of her after we land, in the valley, about midway between Albany and NYC. The conversation is good, largely about media, the shift in what we produce, the loss of proper family entertainment. 

--------

Still at the gate. The flight has been delayed 'til 10 PM ET. A total of 5.5 hours so far. I could keep talking to the girl across from me but I'm losing energy for conversation. I've very much been vaping. Quitting is tomorrow's game. I've watched the sun slide across the sky until everything has become dark. A robot now cleans the airport floors because they've sent all the humans home. There is no recourse for us but quiet starvation. Well, quiet for some. The boomers are milling around, complaining loudly.

I have no recollection of why I started this log. I refuse to reread my work to start trying to trace this into something pithy. I will read Hyperion until the next announcement, probably sending us to hotels. Have a nice evening.

text:
Stories involving AI more commonly had a more humanistic element in the past. A Fire Upon the Deep, Hyperion, Hitchhiker, etc, all involved humans cohabitating a universe where Men went about organic cultural development, in parallel and together with AI, in a way where they were still the center of their worlds, and growth and renaissance was still expected.

The trend of storytelling feels increasingly the total intertwining and eventual replacement of Men with AI, to the point where it becomes unimaginable that humans will live and develop more or less independently, organically, that the actual future of humanity is a story of advancing intelligence (e.g., Pantheon, but consider too the broader narratives by futurists) more so than a humanistic renaissance.

Hell, even the massive pour into the cyberpunk genre is a story about the replacement of organic men by machine, and a struggle with loss of humanity's centering in its own societies. In Cyberpunk 2077, there are AI cities that exist in seclusion, AIs make inroads into human societies, and in cyberspace men exist in an increasingly hedged informational sphere hiding from AIs behind the "Blackwall," a last barrier between overall human society and dangerous wild intelligences. The very march of civilization in that game, further, is about men willingly, passionately dehumanizing themselves, replacing their parts, losing their sense of humanity in chrome. It's a fight on dual planes there.

Which is all to say, the fictional representations of AI continue along the lines of our cultural abandonment of humanism as we find ourselves in a world where it is harder and harder to imagine a proper centering of humans and the utopian development of muscular republican virtues in our own civilizations.

i tumble out of the apartment building and onto the street. i'm with 3 others, all people i know more parasocially than socially, but all of whom i like. we pause and compose ourselves. about one drop of rain hits us every three sconds. it is warm and damp. a couple hugs, then we scatter

the subway is close. it's my usual line, the one that takes me from my front door to my office. minimal walking, very convenient. i descend, pay, descend further, and the convenient digital sign says the train will take 27 minutes to show up. i rip my vape, say fuck it out loud, then return to street level to summon an uber. it is $37. i am willing.

the uber arrives in less than a minute. i bundle myself into it. man is slavic. unknown variety, possibly russian. i thank him. he asks if i just got off work. i tell him kind of. i got off at 7:30. it is now 11:30. I've been making a point of meeting people lately. it's not for my job, but it's not not.

he asks if i'm going about meeting people or meeting girls. i say people, but if people is a girl i will not complain. he laughs. i say i have been having trouble connecting since a heartbreak. he says that is a problem with men in this city. he hears that. that men get their hearts broken and they stop trying. he says i must not stop trying.

i say i don't really stop trying. i just have trouble connecting sometimes. he asks if i want to marry. i say i did. i probably do. i just don't know right now. he says i should marry. he says that young men now, and the gays, they don't have kids. but the way to keep a woman is to have a kid. because love isn't all of a marriage. it is part of a marriage. a woman can get into a fight with a man over anything. a woman wants to fight with a man over anything. and if there is no kid, she can leave him. she will leave him. there is nothing there. with a kid, you have to make it work.

i ask if he is married. he is. he has been for 35 years. he has two children, daughters, 26 and 28. oldest is married. youngest is about to be. i congratulate him. i wow at the length of his marriage. he says it is work. he says you marry someone with a good mother and father who are still together. you marry someone from a good family. he says you have to think of marriage like work. you must wait for the right woman. you are a man, he says, you have time to wait. women after 35 can not have kids. they will come out strange. maybe without a foot. maybe retarded. men can wait until about 50. you should not worry.

he says that you should be thankful that the women in the past broke your heart. there are many women. each one that broke your heart was the wrong woman. that was god keeping you on the right path. if they broke your heart then, the marriage would have been bad. he says that men have weaker hearts than women. he married his best friend's sister. his best friend died 4 days before his wedding. they had to postpone the wedding for a full year, but he eventually married her. his best friend died because of a woman. healthy guy. fine. strong. terrible woman put too much stress on him. one day, he collapsed. that was the end of him. women like to fight. they choose to fight. they can live without a man. they do it all the time. and it's far more often that a husband dies first, rather than the wife. and if the husband dies first, the wife lives much longer. this is because men take things seriously. men fight seriously. it can kill men. it does kill men. it kills them far faster than women, who do not take such things seriously.

we arrive at my apartment. i thank him. he thanks me for the conversation. i step out into the wall of lukewarm humidity. no rain left. i step toward my apartment.
